title: Two Los Angeles albums while still under contract to Tico
summary: On tour in California a label owner asked them to record, and Morris Levy sent a permission letter for two albums.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Okay, before you went to Japan, Macho, you were in Los Angeles, correct? You did two albums there, at the same time. You did The World's Greatest Latin Band and "Machito and the Crescendo". How did that recording come about? Did you go to California with the intent of doing those records?
It just happened while you were there, right?
Yeah, we were there to make a tour of practically every town in, in ....

....and we was there working and the owner of the company come across with us and say: "Gee, I would like to record". We was free, we had finished with --- As a matter of fact, we was signed yet with Tico. We had to send a letter and have the permission for the recording and ----
That's right, because you were with Tico until 1965,'66.
... and he was very nice to allow us to make those ......
Levy, yes. He sent a letter of permission to make those two albums.
Okay, from California you went to Japan?
No, we come back to New York ....
... and then the thing just come about.
I see, but what did you do in New York before you went to Japan?
Oh, we was playing at the Birdland.
